record_notes.DCP-LETT-1735: August 4, 1855, exact header and single XML day; full fifteen paragraphs, 34 footnotes, bibliography, annotations and six raw MathML nodes independently read. P1 acknowledges missing Darwin June 18 letter, referring to own April 20 epistle; catalogue 1670 has April 21, so preserve discrepancy rather than assert exact identity/knowledge date. February outgoing remains separate. Jungle-cock skeleton and some papers intended by same steamer; Somali report hoped not ready and apparatus says actually sent October 8, not August. Blyth explicitly confines observation to Calcutta and reports blocked Ava mission. Trained otters never personally seen and captivity breeding not known; assumptions separate. Rabbits, canaries, geese and cats distinguish personal observation, reports and open questions. Cat types, hybrid ancestry and geography tentative; no general species conclusion assigned to Darwin. P5 half cygnoides; P6/P8 half-bred phrases and P7 two-and-quarter-inch hair are fractions, not 12 or 214. P12 Persian terminology and planned Sanskrit inquiry separate, failure already noted, not completed scholarship. P13 orangutan specimens two received, five en route, further promised; proposed species uncertain. Racial taxonomies, polygenist speculation and value judgments are historical Blyth claims, not present fact or Darwin voice. P14 employment grievance belongs Blyth. Darwin abstract selectively quoted and undated; no three-page abstract fully reproduced. Later Aldrovandi March 1856 reading and publication uses remain future. Worker unlocated-reference sentence incorrectly assigns Hutton extracts to 1735: actual extended Hutton quotations occur in 1746.

P2–6 quoted Hutton observations interspersed with Blyth qualifications; paragraph-level single-speaker labels would misattribute comments. P8 merges closing Blyth signature, Miscellaneous Notes heading, and cat note inside one extraction block; retain internal boundaries. P8–14 enclosure topics and prospective photographs; August 23 dated closing at P15, P16 subsequent P.S. Opening August 22 versus enclosure closing August 23 remains separate; recalled-dispatch story and editorial ordering do not justify an exact reconstructed physical sequence or a single earlier timestamp for whole source. Rüppell travels explicitly never seen (P10), despite consulted Systematische uebersicht; observed Afghan moths not minutely compared (P9); canary cross is inquiry, not confirmed identity. Photography planned next week; wife current daguerreotype work separate. P16 jungle-fowl expected with this mail is prospective and later than August 4 promise; no exact arrival or reading. Future 1860 handwriting comment, later taxonomy and 1867 donation remain apparatus, not contemporaneous knowledge.
